::: {.why}
The distinction is the organising idea of the next two phases, it is not a property of the data, and getting it wrong means either hedging away your edge or holding a risk you are not paid for.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the operational difference between a risk factor and an alpha factor in terms of what you do with the exposure.
- Give one example of a factor that changed category over time and say what moved it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Work the classification through: for each of market, size, value, momentum, low volatility, and your own pairs spread, say whether you would neutralise the exposure or take it, and what evidence would make you switch. The answer depends on whether you are paid for the exposure and on whether your signal is correlated with it by accident.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Demonstrate the accidental exposure: regress your pairs strategy's returns on the four factors and report the loadings with standard errors. Any significant loading is a risk you are running without having decided to.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the classification and the evidence rule into reports/milestone-04-risk-model.md.
:::
:::
